ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture shows a regular hexagon, with a gray six-petal flower-shaped region inside. The six gray petals are rotationally symmetric about the center of the hexagon, and each petal extends from the center of the hexagon to one vertex of the hexagon; the petal boundaries are composed of circular arcs. Taking the right-side petal as an example, its two boundary arcs respectively come from arcs with the upper-right vertex and the lower-right vertex as centers and radius 1. Reasoning: The side length of the regular hexagon is 1, so the distance from the center of the regular hexagon to each vertex is also 1. Consider one petal on the right side; its endpoints are the hexagon center O and the right vertex R, and the centers of the boundary arcs are the upper-right vertex A and the lower-right vertex B. Triangles AOR and BOR are both equilateral triangles with side length 1, so the central angle corresponding to each arc at its center is 60°. One petal consists of two identical circular arc segments. The area of each circular arc segment equals the area of a sector with radius 1 and central angle 60° minus the area of an equilateral triangle with side length 1, namely π/6 - √3/4. Therefore the area of one petal is 2(π/6 - √3/4) = π/3 - √3/2. There are 6 congruent petals in total, so the total area of the gray flower shape is 6(π/3 - √3/2) = 2π - 3√3.
